questions.stem: A firefighter uses a pry bar to lift the edge of a heavy steel plate. The point where the bar rests against a brick acts as the pivot, the firefighter pushes down on the far end, and the plate is the load. In a lever, what is the pivot point called?
questions.rationale: The fixed pivot point of any lever is called the fulcrum. The 'effort' is the force the firefighter applies, not the pivot. The 'load arm' is the distance from the fulcrum to the load, not the pivot itself. 'Mechanical advantage' is the ratio of output force to input force, a property of the system, not a physical point.

questions.stem: A first-class lever has the fulcrum located between the effort and the load (like a seesaw or a pair of pliers). Which of the following everyday tools is also a first-class lever?
questions.rationale: Scissors are a first-class lever: the central pivot (rivet) sits between the effort (your hand) and the load (the material being cut). A wheelbarrow is second-class (load between fulcrum and effort). A fishing rod and a nutcracker are typically third-class and second-class respectively, not first-class.

questions.stem: A firefighter applies effort 4 feet from the fulcrum of a first-class lever to lift a load that sits 1 foot from the fulcrum on the other side. Ignoring the bar's weight, what is the ideal mechanical advantage of this lever?
questions.rationale: Ideal mechanical advantage of a lever equals effort arm length divided by load arm length: 4 ft / 1 ft = 4, or 4 to 1. A 1-to-1 ratio would require equal arms. A 2-to-1 would need a 2 ft effort arm, and 8-to-1 would need an 8 ft effort arm. The longer the effort arm relative to the load arm, the greater the advantage.

questions.stem: On a balanced seesaw (first-class lever), a 150-pound firefighter sits 3 feet from the pivot. A second firefighter weighing 100 pounds sits on the opposite side. To keep the seesaw balanced, how far from the pivot must the 100-pound firefighter sit?
questions.rationale: Balance requires equal torques: weight times distance must match on both sides. 150 lb x 3 ft = 450 ft-lb, so 100 lb x distance = 450, giving distance = 4.5 ft. At 2 ft the torque (200) is too small; at 3 ft (300) still too small; at 5 ft (500) it is too large and would tip toward the lighter firefighter.

questions.stem: A single fixed pulley is mounted at the top of a fire training tower. A firefighter pulls down on a rope to raise a bundle of hose. What is the main benefit of a single fixed pulley?
options: It changes the direction of the applied force
It cuts the required force in half
It triples the speed of lifting
questions.rationale: A single fixed pulley provides a mechanical advantage of 1, so it does not reduce the force needed; its purpose is to change the direction of the force, letting you pull down to lift something up. It does not double force, halve force, or triple speed. To gain a force advantage you need a movable pulley or a block and tackle.

questions.stem: A block and tackle is rigged so that four rope strands directly support a heavy load. Ignoring friction, how much effort force is needed to hold a 400-pound load?
questions.rationale: With four supporting strands, the mechanical advantage is 4, so the effort needed equals the load divided by 4: 400 / 4 = 100 pounds. 200 lb would correspond to a 2-strand system, 400 lb would mean no advantage, and 1,600 lb is the load multiplied rather than divided. Note the rope must be pulled four times as far as the load rises.

questions.stem: Using a block and tackle with a mechanical advantage of 5, a firefighter needs to raise a load a vertical distance of 3 feet. Ignoring friction, how much rope must be pulled through the system?
questions.rationale: In an ideal machine, the distance the effort moves equals the load distance multiplied by the mechanical advantage: 3 ft x 5 = 15 feet of rope. You trade distance for force, so reducing the force fivefold means pulling five times as far. 3 ft ignores the trade-off, 5 ft and 8 ft do not match the 5-to-1 ratio.

questions.stem: Two gears are meshed together so their teeth interlock. If the first gear turns clockwise, which way does the gear directly meshed with it turn?
questions.rationale: When two external gears mesh directly, they always rotate in opposite directions, so a clockwise gear drives its neighbor counterclockwise. It does not turn the same way unless an idler gear sits between them. It will not stay still (the teeth force it to move) and a steadily turning gear does not alternate direction.

questions.stem: A small drive gear with 10 teeth meshes with a larger gear that has 30 teeth. For every one full turn of the larger gear, how many turns does the small gear make?
questions.rationale: The smaller gear turns faster in inverse proportion to the tooth ratio: 30 teeth / 10 teeth = 3, so the small gear makes 3 turns for each turn of the large gear. One-third of a turn describes the large gear's motion per small-gear turn, 1 turn ignores the size difference, and 30 turns confuses tooth count with revolutions.

questions.stem: Three gears are arranged in a line, all meshed in sequence. The first (driver) gear turns clockwise. The middle gear is only an idler. Which direction does the third gear turn?
questions.rationale: Each external mesh reverses direction. The driver turns clockwise, the idler turns counterclockwise, and the third gear reverses again back to clockwise. So the third gear matches the driver. An idler placed in a gear train changes the rotation direction of the output but not its speed, which is why odd numbers of meshing gears end up rotating the same way as the driver.

questions.stem: Pascal's principle states that pressure applied to a confined, incompressible fluid is transmitted equally in all directions. Which piece of firefighting or rescue equipment relies most directly on this principle?
options: A hydraulic rescue spreader (the 'Jaws of Life')
questions.rationale: Hydraulic rescue tools like spreaders use a confined fluid to transmit pressure and multiply force, a direct application of Pascal's principle. A check valve and coiled hose rely on mechanical springs and material flexibility, not pressure multiplication. A gear pump shaft involves rotational mechanics, not Pascal's principle of pressure transmission.

questions.stem: In a hydraulic system, a small piston with an area of 2 square inches has 50 pounds of force pushing on it. A large piston has an area of 20 square inches. Ignoring friction, how much force does the large piston produce?
questions.rationale: Pressure equals force divided by area: 50 lb / 2 sq in = 25 psi, transmitted equally throughout. The large piston output is pressure times its area: 25 psi x 20 sq in = 500 pounds. 50 lb ignores the area difference, 100 lb uses the wrong ratio, and 1,000 lb double-counts the multiplication. The 10-to-1 area ratio gives a 10-to-1 force multiplication.

questions.stem: Pressure is defined as force distributed over an area. If you push with the same total force but spread it over a smaller area, what happens to the pressure?
questions.rationale: Since pressure equals force divided by area, reducing the area while keeping the force constant increases the pressure. This is why a sharp nozzle tip or a narrow blade concentrates force. Pressure does not decrease or stay the same when area shrinks, and it certainly does not drop to zero as long as force is applied.

questions.stem: A hydraulic ram has a piston with a surface area of 5 square inches. The system supplies a pressure of 1,200 psi to the piston. How much force does the piston exert?
questions.rationale: Force equals pressure times area: 1,200 psi x 5 sq in = 6,000 pounds. 240 lb mistakenly divides pressure by area, 1,200 lb ignores the area entirely, and 12,000 lb uses an area of 10 instead of 5. Multiplying pressure by the piston area is the standard way to find the output force of a hydraulic cylinder.

questions.stem: In a hydraulic jack, the input piston is pushed down 10 inches. The output piston, which lifts the load, rises only 1 inch during the same stroke. Assuming an ideal, frictionless system, what is the mechanical advantage?
questions.rationale: In an ideal hydraulic system, mechanical advantage equals the input distance divided by the output distance: 10 in / 1 in = 10, or 10 to 1. Because energy is conserved, moving the input ten times as far means the output force is ten times greater. 1-to-1 ignores the distance difference, 5-to-1 halves the result, and 100-to-1 squares it incorrectly.

questions.stem: Water flows through a fire hose from a pump. If the hose narrows to a smaller diameter at the nozzle while the same amount of water keeps flowing, what happens to the speed of the water at the narrow point?
questions.rationale: When a fixed flow rate passes through a smaller cross-sectional area, the water must speed up to keep the same volume moving per second (the continuity principle). This is exactly why a nozzle accelerates the stream. The water does not slow down or stop, and it cannot keep the same speed because the available area has shrunk.

questions.stem: Two fire hoses are identical in length and supplied at the same pump pressure, but one has twice the inside diameter of the other. Which statement about water flow is correct?
options: Both hoses carry the same volume of water
The larger-diameter hose carries much more water
The smaller-diameter hose carries more water
Diameter has no effect on flow
questions.rationale: A larger-diameter hose has a much greater cross-sectional area and far less friction loss, so it carries substantially more water at the same pressure. Equal volume would only occur with equal diameters. The smaller hose cannot carry more, and diameter strongly affects flow, since friction loss rises sharply as hose diameter decreases.

questions.stem: As water travels through a long fire hose, some pressure is lost along the way. This loss is mainly caused by which of the following?
options: Friction between the water and the hose walls
The water becoming heavier as it flows
The nozzle adding pressure at the end
questions.rationale: Friction loss, the resistance between moving water and the interior hose walls (plus turbulence), is the main reason pressure drops over the length of a hose. Water does not gain mass as it flows, the hose's own weight does not cause pressure loss inside the stream, and a nozzle restricts flow rather than adding pressure to the line.

questions.stem: A wedge, such as the head of an axe or a door chock, is best described as which type of simple machine?
questions.rationale: A wedge is essentially a moving inclined plane (or two inclined planes back to back) that converts a forward force into sideways splitting force. It is not a pulley (which uses rope and wheels), not a gear (which uses meshing teeth), and not a lever (which pivots on a fulcrum). Firefighters use wedges and chocks to hold doors and split materials.

questions.stem: A firefighter raises an extension ladder against a wall. Compared with standing it straight up, what is the main mechanical benefit of leaning the ladder at an angle so it acts like an inclined plane for climbing?
options: It lets the firefighter climb with less effort over a greater distance
It removes the firefighter's weight entirely
It makes the ladder weigh less
It increases the ladder's height beyond its length
questions.rationale: An inclined plane (the leaning ladder) lets you reach a height with less effort at any instant by spreading the climb over a longer path, trading distance for reduced effort. It does not remove the climber's weight, change the ladder's actual weight, or make the ladder reach higher than its own length, since a leaned ladder reaches lower than when vertical.

questions.stem: A gate valve in a water main is opened by turning a handwheel connected to a threaded screw stem. The screw advances 0.25 inch for each full turn of the handwheel, whose rim travels about 12 inches per turn. Ignoring friction, this screw mechanism provides an approximate mechanical advantage of:
questions.rationale: A screw's ideal mechanical advantage equals the distance the effort travels in one turn divided by the distance the load advances (the pitch): 12 in / 0.25 in = 48, or about 48 to 1. This is why a small turning effort can produce a large clamping or sealing force. 3-to-1 and 12-to-1 understate it, and 0.25-to-1 inverts the ratio.

questions.stem: A nozzle reduces a hose stream from a 2-inch inside diameter down to a 1-inch inside diameter. Because flow rate stays constant, by approximately what factor does the water's velocity increase at the smaller opening? (Hint: area depends on the square of the diameter.)
questions.rationale: Cross-sectional area scales with the square of the diameter, so halving the diameter from 2 in to 1 in reduces the area to one-fourth. To keep the same flow rate, velocity must increase by 4 times. A factor of 2 mistakenly uses the diameter ratio directly, 3 times has no basis, and the velocity certainly changes because the opening is much smaller.

questions.stem: A firefighter uses a long-handled spanner wrench to loosen a tight hose coupling. Why does a longer handle make the coupling easier to turn?
options: It reduces the weight of the coupling
It increases the torque for the same hand force
It lowers the friction inside the coupling
It changes the direction the coupling turns
questions.rationale: Torque equals force times the distance from the pivot, so a longer handle increases the turning effect (torque) for the same hand force, making the coupling easier to break loose. The handle length does not change the coupling's weight, does not reduce internal friction, and does not change which direction you turn it. This is the lever principle applied to rotation.

questions.stem: A firefighter must move a 200-pound piece of equipment up to a truck bed. Which method requires the LEAST effort force, assuming all are frictionless and ideal?
options: Lifting it straight up by hand
Pushing it up a long, gently sloped ramp
Pushing it up a short, steep ramp
questions.rationale: A long, gently sloped ramp is an inclined plane with high mechanical advantage, so it requires the least effort force (though over a longer distance). Lifting straight up requires the full 200-pound force. A short steep ramp has a smaller mechanical advantage and needs more force. Throwing it adds force rather than reducing it. The gentler the slope, the less force needed.

questions.stem:
DEPARTMENTAL MEMO: Effective Monday, all engine companies must complete a daily inspection of self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) units before 0800 hours. Crew members shall verify that each cylinder reads at least 90 percent of full capacity. Any unit that fails inspection must be tagged out of service and reported to the shift captain immediately. Replacement units are stored in the second-floor equipment room.

According to the memo, what must a crew member do if an SCBA unit fails inspection?
options: Refill the cylinder to 90 percent capacity
Tag the unit out of service and report it to the shift captain
Move the unit to the second-floor equipment room
Wait until after 0800 hours to retest the unit
questions.rationale: The memo states that any unit that fails inspection 'must be tagged out of service and reported to the shift captain immediately,' making choice B correct. Choice A is wrong because the memo never instructs crew members to refill cylinders themselves. Choice C confuses the storage location of replacement units with the action for a failed unit. Choice D contradicts the memo, which requires inspections before 0800, not retesting afterward.

questions.stem:
SAFETY BULLETIN: Recent incident reviews show that injuries during overhaul often occur after the visible fire is out. Crews can become complacent once flames are no longer present, removing protective gear too early. Hidden embers, weakened floors, and lingering toxic gases remain serious hazards during this phase. Supervisors must keep full personal protective equipment in place until air monitoring confirms the area is safe.

What is the main idea of this bulletin?
options: Flames are the most dangerous part of any fire
Air monitoring equipment is frequently unreliable
The overhaul phase remains hazardous even after visible fire is gone
Protective gear should be removed as soon as flames disappear
questions.rationale: The bulletin's central point is that danger continues during overhaul after flames are gone, supported by references to hidden embers, weakened floors, and toxic gases; choice C captures this. Choice A is contradicted because the bulletin warns about hazards after flames are out. Choice B is not discussed; the bulletin treats air monitoring as a safety tool, not an unreliable one. Choice D states the dangerous complacent behavior the bulletin warns against, not its message.

Choice A is the opposite of complacent. Choice C introduces confusion, which the passage does not mention. Choice D refers to fatigue, but the bulletin describes a false sense of safety, not tiredness.

questions.stem:
INCIDENT REPORT EXCERPT: At 0214 hours, Engine 7 arrived at a single-story residence with smoke showing from the rear. The homeowner reported that all occupants were accounted for in the front yard. The officer ordered a defensive exterior attack rather than entry, citing heavy fire involvement in the rear and a sagging roofline. Crews knocked down the visible fire from outside before performing a limited interior survey once conditions stabilized.

Which statement is the best inference about why the officer chose a defensive exterior attack?
options: The officer believed an interior attack posed too great a structural risk with no lives to save
The engine company lacked enough water to fight the fire
The homeowner specifically requested an exterior attack
Department policy forbids interior attacks at night
questions.rationale: The report notes all occupants were accounted for and cites a 'sagging roofline' and heavy rear fire, so a reasonable inference is that the collapse risk outweighed any need to enter for rescue, making choice A correct. Choice B is unsupported; water supply is never mentioned. Choice C is wrong because the homeowner only reported occupant status, not tactics. Choice D invents a policy not stated in the report.

questions.stem:
EQUIPMENT MANUAL: The thermal imaging camera (TIC) should be powered on and allowed to calibrate for ten seconds before use. Point the lens away from direct heat sources during calibration to avoid inaccurate readings. The display uses a color palette in which warmer surfaces appear lighter and cooler surfaces appear darker. Replace the battery whenever the indicator shows fewer than two bars.

According to the manual, how do warmer surfaces appear on the TIC display?
questions.rationale: The manual states the palette makes 'warmer surfaces appear lighter and cooler surfaces appear darker,' so choice B is correct. Choice A reverses this relationship. Choices C and D describe display behaviors (red outlines, blinking) that the manual never mentions.

questions.stem:
STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE: Upon arriving first at a motor vehicle collision, the company officer shall establish command and conduct a 360-degree size-up. Before any crew approaches the vehicles, the apparatus shall be positioned to shield the work area from oncoming traffic. Only after traffic control is in place may crews begin patient assessment and extrication. Power lines, leaking fluids, and vehicle stability must be evaluated and reported during the size-up.

What is the author's primary purpose in this SOP?
options: To explain how to repair damaged vehicles after a collision
To establish a safe, ordered sequence of actions at a vehicle collision scene
To list the equipment carried on a rescue apparatus
To describe the causes of motor vehicle collisions
questions.rationale: The SOP lays out a required order of operations, from establishing command to positioning the apparatus to beginning extrication, so its purpose is to define a safe, ordered sequence, making choice B correct. Choice A is wrong because the SOP concerns scene safety, not vehicle repair. Choice C is incorrect; no equipment list appears. Choice D is unsupported, as causes of collisions are never discussed.

questions.stem:
TRAINING NOTICE: All probationary firefighters must log a minimum of 40 hours of hose-handling drills during their first quarter. Hours completed under direct supervision of a certified instructor count double toward this requirement. Probationers should record each session in the online training portal by the end of the same shift. Unrecorded hours will not be credited.

A probationer completes 12 hours of supervised drills with a certified instructor and 6 hours of unsupervised drills, recording all of them on time. How many credited hours does the probationer have?
questions.rationale: Supervised hours count double, so 12 supervised hours equal 24 credited hours; adding the 6 unsupervised hours gives 30 credited hours, making choice C correct. Choice A (18) simply sums the raw hours without doubling. Choice B (24) counts only the doubled supervised hours and ignores the unsupervised hours. Choice D (36) incorrectly doubles all hours.

questions.stem:
INCIDENT REPORT EXCERPT: Ladder 3 responded to a reported odor of natural gas in a commercial kitchen. Upon arrival, the crew detected elevated gas readings near a wall-mounted oven. They evacuated the building, ventilated the space, and shut off the main gas valve. The utility company was notified to inspect and restore service. No ignition source was activated by crews during the operation.

Why did the crew most likely avoid activating any ignition source during the operation?
options: To conserve electrical power in the building
To prevent the accumulated gas from igniting
Because the utility company had not yet arrived
To preserve evidence for an investigation
questions.rationale: Given elevated natural gas readings, the most reasonable inference is that crews avoided ignition sources to prevent the gas from igniting and causing an explosion, so choice B is correct. Choice A misreads the action as energy conservation. Choice C confuses notification with a cause for avoiding ignition. Choice D introduces an investigation purpose not supported by the gas-leak context.

questions.stem:
DEPARTMENTAL POLICY: The department reimburses firefighters for approved continuing-education courses at a rate of $20 per classroom hour, up to a maximum of $400 per calendar year. Online self-study courses are reimbursed at half the classroom rate. Receipts and a completion certificate must be submitted within 30 days of finishing a course to qualify for reimbursement.

A firefighter completes a 10-hour online self-study course and submits the proper paperwork on time. How much will the firefighter be reimbursed?
questions.rationale: Online courses pay half the $20 classroom rate, or $10 per hour; 10 hours at $10 equals $100, so choice B is correct. Choice A would result from an incorrect $5 rate. Choice C uses the full classroom rate of $20 instead of the half rate for online courses. Choice D is the annual maximum, not the amount earned for this course.

questions.stem:
SAFETY BULLETIN: Rehabilitation, or 'rehab,' is not a sign of weakness but a critical operational function. After strenuous activity, firefighters must rotate to the rehab area to rest, rehydrate, and have vital signs checked. A firefighter whose heart rate or temperature remains elevated after rest may not return to active duty until cleared by medical personnel. Treating rehab as optional places both the individual and the crew at risk.

What tone does the author take toward firefighters who view rehab as optional?
options: Approving, because experienced firefighters can judge their own limits
Disapproving, because skipping rehab endangers the firefighter and the crew
Indifferent, because rehab is purely a personal choice
Amused, because the concern is exaggerated
questions.rationale: The bulletin states that 'treating rehab as optional places both the individual and the crew at risk,' signaling clear disapproval of skipping rehab, so choice B is correct. Choice A contradicts the requirement that firefighters be medically cleared. Choice C is wrong because the bulletin frames rehab as a required 'operational function,' not a personal choice. Choice D misreads the serious tone as humor.

In this passage, the word 'snug' most nearly means:
questions.rationale: The sentence describes tightening the coupling by hand 'then snug it with a spanner wrench,' indicating snug means to tighten it firmly, so choice B is correct. Choice A is the opposite action. Choice C contradicts the goal of securing the coupling. Choice D describes inspection, not the tightening action implied by using a wrench.

questions.stem: A fire engine carries 500 gallons of water in its tank. During a small grass fire, the crew uses 175 gallons. How many gallons remain in the tank?
questions.rationale: Subtract the water used from the tank capacity: 500 - 175 = 325 gallons remaining.

questions.stem: A fire station has 6 firefighters per shift and runs 4 shifts to cover a full rotation. How many firefighter positions are needed to fill all shifts?
questions.rationale: Multiply firefighters per shift by number of shifts: 6 x 4 = 24 positions.

questions.stem: A ladder truck responds to 3 calls on Monday, 5 calls on Tuesday, and 4 calls on Wednesday. What is the total number of calls over these three days?
questions.rationale: Add the calls for each day: 3 + 5 + 4 = 12 total calls.

questions.stem: A single section of fire hose is 50 feet long. If a crew connects 7 sections together, what is the total length of the hose line?
questions.rationale: Multiply the length of one section by the number of sections: 50 x 7 = 350 feet.

questions.stem: A water tank holds 1,200 gallons. The crew has already filled it to 3/4 of its capacity. How many gallons are currently in the tank?
questions.rationale: Multiply the capacity by 3/4: 1,200 x 3 = 3,600, then 3,600 / 4 = 900 gallons.

questions.stem: A fire hose discharges water at a rate of 125 gallons per minute (GPM). How many gallons will it discharge in 8 minutes?
questions.rationale: Multiply the flow rate by the time: 125 GPM x 8 minutes = 1,000 gallons.

questions.stem: A pump moves 1,800 gallons of water in 12 minutes at a steady rate. What is its flow rate in gallons per minute (GPM)?
questions.rationale: Divide the total gallons by the time: 1,800 / 12 = 150 GPM.

questions.stem: On a written exam, a candidate answers 68 of 80 questions correctly. What percentage did the candidate score?
questions.rationale: Divide correct by total and multiply by 100: 68 / 80 = 0.85, and 0.85 x 100 = 85%.

questions.stem: A fire department's equipment budget of $24,000 is increased by 15% for the next year. What is the new budget?
Four engine companies recorded the following response times in minutes: 6, 9, 7, and 10. What is the average response time?
questions.rationale: Add the times: 6 + 9 + 7 + 10 = 32. Divide by the count: 32 / 4 = 8 minutes.

questions.stem: A foam concentrate is mixed with water in a ratio of 1 part foam to 24 parts water. To make 100 gallons of finished solution, how many gallons of foam concentrate are needed?
questions.rationale: The ratio 1:24 means 25 total parts per batch. The foam fraction is 1/25. Multiply: 100 x (1/25) = 4 gallons of concentrate.

questions.stem: If 3 firefighters can clean and repack 12 hose lines in one hour, how many hose lines can 5 firefighters repack in one hour at the same rate?
questions.rationale: Find the rate per firefighter: 12 / 3 = 4 lines each. Multiply by 5 firefighters: 4 x 5 = 20 hose lines.

questions.stem: A hose line is 0.25 mile long. There are 5,280 feet in a mile. How many feet long is the hose line?
questions.rationale: Multiply the fraction of a mile by feet per mile: 0.25 x 5,280 = 1,320 feet.

questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to the decimal 0.75?
questions.rationale: The decimal 0.75 means 75 hundredths: 75/100. Dividing numerator and denominator by 25 gives 3/4.

questions.stem: A rectangular water tank measures 10 feet long, 6 feet wide, and 4 feet deep. If 1 cubic foot holds about 7.48 gallons, approximately how many gallons does the full tank hold?
questions.rationale: Find the volume: 10 x 6 x 4 = 240 cubic feet. Multiply by gallons per cubic foot: 240 x 7.48 = 1,795.2, about 1,795 gallons.

questions.stem: A station floor is a rectangle 30 feet long and 20 feet wide. What is the area of the floor in square feet?
questions.rationale: Area of a rectangle is length times width: 30 x 20 = 600 square feet.

questions.rationale: Subtract 7 from both sides: 3x = 18. Divide both sides by 3: x = 6.

questions.stem: Solve for x: (x / 4) - 3 = 9.
questions.rationale: Add 3 to both sides: x / 4 = 12. Multiply both sides by 4: x = 48.

questions.stem: A fire apparatus travels at a steady 45 miles per hour. How many miles does it travel in 20 minutes?
questions.rationale: 20 minutes is 20/60 = 1/3 of an hour. Multiply speed by time: 45 x (1/3) = 15 miles.

questions.stem: A 750-gallon tank is being drained at 30 gallons per minute while simultaneously being filled at 5 gallons per minute. How many minutes will it take to empty the tank?
questions.rationale: Net drain rate is 30 - 5 = 25 gallons per minute. Divide the volume by the net rate: 750 / 25 = 30 minutes.

questions.stem: Two pumps fill a reservoir. Pump A delivers 90 GPM and Pump B delivers 60 GPM. Working together, how long will it take them to deliver 4,500 gallons?
questions.rationale: Combined rate is 90 + 60 = 150 GPM. Divide total gallons by combined rate: 4,500 / 150 = 30 minutes.

questions.stem: A department buys 8 self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) units at $4,250 each. What is the total cost?
questions.rationale: Multiply the unit price by the quantity: 4,250 x 8 = $34,000.

questions.stem: A fire alarm system normally priced at $1,800 is on sale for 20% off. After the discount, an 8% sales tax is applied. What is the final price?
A pumper must supply 350 GPM for 25 minutes to control a structure fire. Its onboard tank holds 500 gallons, and the rest is drawn from a hydrant. How many gallons must the hydrant supply?
questions.rationale: Total water needed: 350 GPM x 25 minutes = 8,750 gallons. Subtract the tank's 500 gallons: 8,750 - 500 = 8,250 gallons from the hydrant.

questions.stem: You are facing north. You turn 90 degrees to your right. Which direction are you now facing?
questions.rationale: Starting at north and turning 90 degrees clockwise (to the right) brings you to east. The clockwise order is north, east, south, west, so one right turn from north lands on east.

questions.stem: You are facing south. You make two right turns of 90 degrees each. Which direction are you now facing?
questions.rationale: Each 90-degree right turn moves you one step clockwise. From south, one right turn gives west, and a second right turn gives north. Two right turns total 180 degrees, which is the opposite of south, confirming north.

questions.stem: A fire engine is driving east. The driver makes a left turn at an intersection. In which direction is the engine now traveling?
questions.rationale: A left turn is 90 degrees counterclockwise. Going clockwise the order is north, east, south, west; turning left (counterclockwise) from east moves you back one step to north.

questions.stem: You start by walking 3 blocks north, then turn and walk 4 blocks east, then turn and walk 3 blocks south. In which direction is your starting point relative to your current position?
questions.rationale: Walking 3 blocks north then 3 blocks south cancels out, leaving no net north-south change. The only remaining movement is 4 blocks east, so you end up 4 blocks east of your start. Therefore the starting point lies directly west of where you are now.

questions.stem: Facing west, you turn 180 degrees, then make one left turn of 90 degrees. Which direction are you now facing?
questions.rationale: Facing west, a 180-degree turn leaves you facing east. A left turn is 90 degrees counterclockwise; turning left from east brings you to north (the counterclockwise order is east, north, west, south). So you end up facing north.

questions.stem: Two firefighters stand facing each other. The first firefighter raises the hand on his own right side. From the second firefighter's point of view (who is facing him), on which side does the raised hand appear?
questions.rationale: When two people face each other, their left and right are mirrored. The first firefighter's right hand is on the side that, from the facing observer's viewpoint, appears on the observer's left. So it appears on the second firefighter's left.

questions.stem: You enter a building through the south door into a lobby. Straight ahead (north) is a hallway. The first room on the right side of the hallway is the equipment room. After walking north down the hallway, on which compass side of the hallway is the equipment room located?
questions.rationale: Entering from the south and walking north means you are facing north. When facing north, your right hand points east. The first room on your right is therefore on the east side of the hallway.

questions.stem: On a grid of one-way streets, traffic on Main Street flows only eastbound and traffic on 1st Avenue flows only northbound. You are driving and need to legally travel from the southwest corner of the Main/1st intersection to a point two blocks east and one block north. Which legal first move is possible?
questions.rationale: Main Street only allows eastbound travel and 1st Avenue only allows northbound travel. Since you must reach a point that is both east and north, and your only legal directions are east (on Main) and north (on 1st), driving east on Main Street is a valid first move. Driving west or south violates the one-way restrictions, and you cannot drive north on Main Street because Main runs east-west.

questions.stem: A ladder leans against a wall. Looking at the ladder from the front, the top of the ladder tilts toward the left. If you walk around and view the same ladder from directly behind the wall, toward which side does the top of the ladder now appear to tilt?
questions.rationale: Viewing an object from the opposite side reverses the left-right orientation, like looking in a mirror. A tilt to the left from the front becomes a tilt to the right when seen from behind.

questions.stem: You walk 5 blocks north, then 2 blocks west, then 5 blocks south, then 2 blocks east. Where are you relative to your starting point?
questions.rationale: The 5 blocks north and 5 blocks south cancel each other, and the 2 blocks west and 2 blocks east cancel each other. With no net movement in any direction, you return exactly to your starting point.

questions.stem: Facing north, you make the following turns in order: right, then right, then left, then right. Which direction are you facing at the end?
questions.rationale: Count each right turn as +90 degrees (clockwise) and each left turn as -90 degrees. The turns total +90 +90 -90 +90 = +180 degrees. Starting from north, a net 180-degree turn leaves you facing south.

questions.stem: A floor plan shows a square room with one exit on each wall: north, south, east, and west. You are standing in the room facing the west exit. The exit directly behind you leads to which compass direction?
questions.rationale: If you face west, the direction directly behind you is the opposite of west, which is east. The exit behind you is therefore the east exit.

questions.stem: To assemble a hose connection correctly, the steps must follow this order: (1) inspect the gasket, (2) align the threads, (3) hand-tighten the coupling, (4) wrench-tighten the coupling. A trainee starts by aligning the threads. Which step did the trainee skip, and what should have come first?
questions.rationale: The correct sequence begins with inspecting the gasket (step 1) before aligning the threads (step 2). By starting with aligning the threads, the trainee skipped the first step, which is inspecting the gasket.

questions.stem: You are at the center of a building's ground floor. The nearest stairwell is 30 feet to your north. The nearest exterior exit is 20 feet to your east. A second exterior exit is 50 feet to your west. Smoke blocks everything to the north. To reach the closest usable exterior exit, which way should you go and how far?
questions.rationale: The stairwell to the north is blocked by smoke, so it is not usable. Between the two usable exterior exits, the east exit is 20 feet away and the west exit is 50 feet away. The east exit is closer, so you should travel east 20 feet.

questions.stem: A driver is heading north and makes three consecutive left turns of 90 degrees each. Which direction is the driver facing after the three turns?
questions.rationale: Each left turn is 90 degrees counterclockwise. From north: first left gives west, second left gives south, third left gives east. Three left turns equal 270 degrees counterclockwise, which is the same as one right turn (90 degrees clockwise) from north, landing on east.

questions.stem: Looking at a person who is facing you and waving with the hand on your right, which of that person's hands is waving?
questions.rationale: Because the person faces you, their orientation is mirrored relative to yours. The hand that appears on your right side is actually on the person's left side, so they are waving their left hand.

questions.stem: On a city grid, you begin at the corner of 2nd Street and Oak Avenue. Streets run east-west and avenues run north-south. You travel 3 blocks east along 2nd Street, turn left and travel 2 blocks, then turn left and travel 1 block. Relative to your starting corner, where are you now?
questions.rationale: Start facing east, travel 3 blocks east. Turn left (now facing north), travel 2 blocks north. Turn left again (now facing west), travel 1 block west. Net east-west: 3 east minus 1 west equals 2 blocks east. Net north-south: 2 blocks north. So you are 2 blocks east and 2 blocks north of the start.

questions.stem: A rectangular fire station has its main apparatus bay door on the south wall. A fire engine pulls straight out of the bay heading south, then immediately turns to its right to head down the street. In which direction is the engine now traveling?
questions.rationale: The engine exits heading south. A turn to its right is 90 degrees clockwise relative to its direction of travel. When facing south, your right side points west, so after turning right the engine travels west.

questions.stem: A square emergency placard has the word 'TOP' printed along its upper edge when held upright. The placard is rotated 90 degrees clockwise and mounted on a wall. After this rotation, along which edge of the placard does the word 'TOP' now sit?
questions.rationale: Rotating an object 90 degrees clockwise moves whatever was on the top edge to the right edge. Picture a clock: the 12 position (top) moves to the 3 position (right) after a quarter turn clockwise. So the word 'TOP' now sits along the right edge.

questions.stem: You drive 6 miles east, then 8 miles north. As the crow flies, how far are you from your starting point?
questions.rationale: The east leg and north leg are perpendicular, forming the two legs of a right triangle. The straight-line distance is the hypotenuse: the square root of (6 squared plus 8 squared) equals the square root of (36 plus 64) equals the square root of 100, which is 10 miles. This is the classic 6-8-10 right triangle.

questions.stem: During a kitchen-fire response, your company officer assigns you to pull and stretch the attack line while another firefighter forces the rear door. You believe it would be faster to enter through the front. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Quietly abandon your assignment and go in through the front door on your own.
Carry out your assigned task of stretching the attack line, and raise your idea with the officer afterward if it is still relevant.
Stop and argue with the officer about entry points while the fire grows.
Refuse to move until the officer agrees to use the front door.
questions.rationale: On the fireground, freelancing is dangerous and breaks the coordinated plan that keeps the crew safe; you complete your assigned task and offer suggestions through the chain of command at an appropriate time. Abandoning your assignment, arguing, or refusing all undermine teamwork, waste critical time, and put the crew at risk.

questions.stem: You notice that a fellow recruit consistently skips checking the SCBA air-pressure gauge during morning equipment inspections. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Say nothing because it is not your assigned equipment.
Report the recruit directly to the fire chief without speaking to anyone else first.
Privately remind the recruit that the air-pressure check is required for safety, and if it continues, raise it with your officer.
Tamper with the recruit's SCBA so they learn a lesson.
questions.rationale: Safety-critical checks protect lives, so the issue must be addressed; a respectful peer reminder is the appropriate first step, escalating through your supervisor if it continues. Staying silent ignores a real hazard, jumping straight to the chief skips the chain of command, and tampering is dangerous and unethical.

questions.stem: While responding to a medical call, an elderly resident becomes upset and yells that your crew is taking too long and is incompetent. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Yell back to assert your authority and tell the resident to calm down.
Stay calm, acknowledge the resident's frustration, and continue providing professional care while explaining what you are doing.
Threaten to leave if the resident does not stop complaining.
Ignore the resident completely and refuse to speak to them.
questions.rationale: Calm professionalism and empathy de-escalate distressed members of the public while care continues uninterrupted. Yelling back, threatening to leave, and ignoring the person all escalate the situation and conflict with the firefighter's public-service and customer-service responsibilities.

questions.stem: You accidentally damage a piece of station equipment while cleaning it, and no one else saw it happen. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Put the equipment back and say nothing, hoping no one notices.
Blame the previous shift so you do not get in trouble.
Hide the damaged equipment in a storage closet.
Report the damage promptly to your officer and explain what happened.
questions.rationale: Integrity requires honest, prompt reporting so the equipment can be repaired or replaced before it is needed at an emergency. Concealing the damage, blaming others, or hiding the equipment are dishonest and could leave the crew with faulty gear at a critical moment.

questions.stem: Your officer gives an order during overhaul that you are almost certain violates a safety procedure you were recently trained on. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Refuse the order loudly in front of the whole crew and walk away.
Carry out the order exactly as given without saying anything, since the officer outranks you.
Respectfully and promptly voice your specific safety concern to the officer before acting, so it can be clarified or corrected.
Pretend to comply but secretly do something different.
questions.rationale: The chain of command expects members to follow orders, but safety concerns should be raised respectfully and immediately so they can be addressed; this preserves both safety and discipline. Publicly refusing undermines authority, blind compliance with a genuine safety risk endangers the crew, and secretly doing your own thing is dangerous freelancing.

questions.stem: Two firefighters on your crew have an ongoing personal disagreement that is starting to affect how they work together on calls. You are their peer. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Take the side of the firefighter you like better and help them win the argument.
Encourage them to resolve it professionally, and if it keeps affecting performance and safety, bring it to your officer's attention.
Spread the details of the conflict to the rest of the station.
Ignore it entirely, even though it is affecting calls.
questions.rationale: Crew cohesion is essential to safe operations, so you encourage a professional resolution and escalate to leadership if performance or safety is being affected. Taking sides and gossiping worsen the conflict, and ignoring a problem that is degrading performance on calls fails the team and the public.

questions.stem: After a difficult rescue, a local news reporter approaches you at the scene and asks you to confirm details about the victim's condition and the cause of the fire. You do not have official authorization to speak to media. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Share everything you know to make the department look responsive.
Politely decline to comment and refer the reporter to your officer or the department's public information officer.
Give the reporter unofficial details but ask them not to quote you.
Make up an answer so you do not seem unhelpful.
questions.rationale: Releasing scene information is the role of authorized personnel such as a public information officer; politely deferring protects accuracy, privacy, and the investigation. Sharing details, going off the record, or fabricating information all risk spreading false or confidential information and violate department protocol.

questions.stem: It is a slow shift at the station and you have completed your assigned duties. Your officer has not given you a new task. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Sit down to watch television and wait until someone tells you to do something.
Look for productive work such as training, equipment checks, or station upkeep, or ask your officer if anything needs doing.
Leave the station to run personal errands since there are no calls.
Tell newer members to do all the remaining chores for you.
questions.rationale: A strong work ethic and initiative mean using downtime for training, maintenance, and readiness rather than waiting to be told. Idling, leaving without authorization, and offloading your work onto others reflect poor professionalism and reduce the crew's readiness.

questions.stem: A coworker tells an offensive joke that targets a particular ethnic group while the crew is eating dinner. You find it inappropriate. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Laugh along so you are not seen as difficult.
Calmly make clear the joke is not acceptable, and report it through proper channels if the behavior continues.
Tell an offensive joke of your own to even things out.
Say nothing and simply avoid that coworker in the future.
questions.rationale: The fire service requires a respectful, discrimination-free workplace; addressing the comment and escalating if needed upholds that standard. Laughing along condones the behavior, retaliating with another offensive joke makes it worse, and silent avoidance allows a hostile environment to persist.

questions.stem: During a structure fire, your assigned partner suddenly tells you over the radio that they are low on air and feeling disoriented. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Continue your own task and tell them to find their own way out.
Immediately notify command, stay with your partner, and help guide them to safety following your training.
Remove your own mask to share air without alerting anyone.
Speed up your task so the crew can finish before your partner runs out of air.
questions.rationale: Firefighters never abandon a partner in distress; alerting command and assisting their exit per training protects both members. Telling them to manage alone, removing your own mask in a hazardous atmosphere, or prioritizing the task over a member's life all violate crew-safety and accountability principles.

questions.stem: A member of the public walks into the station and asks for help installing a smoke detector in their home. There are no active calls. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Tell them the fire department is only for emergencies and send them away.
Respond helpfully, explain the department's process for smoke-detector assistance, and connect them with the right program or personnel.
Tell them to figure it out themselves using an online video.
Charge them a personal fee to come help.
questions.rationale: Public education and fire prevention are core fire-service functions, and a customer-service mindset means helping residents access these programs. Dismissing the request, brushing them off, or charging a personal fee neglect the department's public-service mission and damage community trust.

questions.stem: You suspect that a senior, well-liked firefighter has been falsifying hours on equipment-maintenance logs, signing off on checks that were not actually performed. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Confront the firefighter in front of the whole crew to embarrass them.
Ignore it because the firefighter is popular and senior to you.
Falsify your own logs too, since apparently everyone does it.
Report your specific, factual concerns through the proper chain of command and let leadership investigate.
questions.rationale: Falsified safety logs can lead to equipment failures that endanger lives, so factual concerns must be reported through proper channels regardless of the person's popularity or rank. Public confrontation is unprofessional and unfair, ignoring it allows a serious hazard, and falsifying your own logs compounds the misconduct.

questions.stem: On scene at a car accident, a bystander begins filming closely and gets in the way of your crew treating a patient. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Grab the bystander's phone and delete the video.
Calmly and firmly ask the bystander to step back for everyone's safety, and request scene control from police if needed.
Stop treating the patient until the bystander leaves.
Get into a shouting match with the bystander about their rights.
questions.rationale: Maintaining a safe work area while staying professional is the priority; politely directing the bystander back and using law enforcement for scene control balances patient care with public relations. Seizing property is unlawful, halting treatment harms the patient, and arguing escalates the situation and wastes time.

questions.stem: Your officer asks the crew to complete a thorough cleaning of the apparatus bay, but you think the task is beneath your skills as a trained firefighter. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Refuse and remind everyone you trained for emergencies, not chores.
Do a deliberately poor job so you are not asked again.
Complete the task properly as part of your shared responsibility for the station.
Convince a junior member to do your portion while you rest.
questions.rationale: Station maintenance is a shared duty, and completing all assigned tasks well reflects professionalism and team commitment regardless of skill level. Refusing, doing intentionally poor work, or offloading the task onto others undermine teamwork and show poor attitude.

questions.stem: You are dispatched to a false-alarm call at the same address for the third time this week. The resident seems lonely and apologetic. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Scold the resident for wasting the department's time.
Respond professionally, check the alarm, and consider whether the resident needs a referral to support services or alarm maintenance.
Disconnect the resident's alarm so it stops calling you.
Tell dispatch to stop sending your crew to that address.
questions.rationale: Every call is treated professionally, and recurring calls may signal an equipment problem or a resident who needs help, warranting a thoughtful response and possible referral. Scolding the resident, disabling a life-safety device, or refusing future response neglect duty and could leave the resident in danger.

questions.stem: You arrive first at a small kitchen fire and the homeowner, in a panic, urges you to rush in immediately before your backup and water supply are established. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Rush in alone right away to satisfy the homeowner.
Reassure the homeowner while you size up the scene and follow safe procedures for backup, water supply, and crew coordination before entry.
Tell the homeowner the fire is their own fault and wait outside.
Leave the scene to avoid the risk entirely.
questions.rationale: Safety procedures, scene size-up, and proper support reduce the risk of injury or death; reassuring the homeowner while following protocol balances compassion with safety. Rushing in unsupported endangers you and the crew, blaming the homeowner is unprofessional, and abandoning the scene fails the public-service duty.

questions.stem: A more experienced firefighter offers you feedback that your hose-handling technique is sloppy and could be improved. You worked hard on it and feel defensive. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Dismiss the feedback because you already did your best.
Listen openly, thank them, and use the feedback to improve your technique.
Tell them their own technique is no better.
Complain to other members that the firefighter is picking on you.
questions.rationale: Receiving constructive feedback with an open mind drives continuous improvement and stronger team performance. Dismissing the input, deflecting with criticism, or complaining to others reflect poor coachability and harm both your development and crew relationships.

questions.stem: You realize you are running late for the start of your shift, which means the off-going crew cannot leave until you arrive. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Take your time since the off-going crew is still there to cover.
Notify your supervisor or station as soon as you know you will be late, and make every reasonable effort to arrive promptly.
Arrive late without telling anyone and act as if nothing happened.
Ask a friend to clock in for you so it looks like you were on time.
questions.rationale: Reliability and communication matter because shifts depend on timely relief; notifying the station and hurrying responsibly shows accountability. Taking your time disrespects the off-going crew, saying nothing leaves them uninformed, and having someone clock in for you is dishonest.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be the LEAST appropriate action when you discover that a teammate forgot to restock essential medical supplies on the rig before a shift?
options: Restock the missing supplies right away so the rig is ready for the next call.
Quietly let the teammate know so they can avoid the mistake next time.
Publicly criticize the teammate in front of the crew and report them to discourage anyone from making errors.
Confirm with your officer that the restocking procedure is clear for everyone.
questions.rationale: This question asks for the LEAST appropriate action. Publicly criticizing a teammate over an honest mistake damages morale and trust without improving readiness, so it is the worst option. Promptly restocking, giving a quiet heads-up, and clarifying the procedure all fix the immediate problem and prevent recurrence in a constructive way.

questions.stem: At the scene of a multi-vehicle crash, you must help triage several patients but resources are limited until additional units arrive. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Treat the first patient you reach completely before assessing anyone else.
Follow established triage procedures to assess all patients quickly and prioritize care based on severity and survivability.
Focus only on the patient who is shouting the loudest.
Wait for all additional units to arrive before doing anything.
questions.rationale: Triage protocols are designed to do the most good for the most people when resources are limited, so rapid assessment and severity-based prioritization is correct. Fully treating one patient first, responding to the loudest voice, or waiting idly all leave critical patients untreated and waste scarce time.

questions.stem: A close friend who is also a firefighter asks you to cover for them by not mentioning that they showed up to a recent call smelling of alcohol. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Agree to stay quiet because they are your friend.
Decline to cover it up and report the safety concern through the proper channels, even though it is difficult.
Warn the friend to hide it better next time.
Bring it up casually with other crew members but not leadership.
questions.rationale: A firefighter impaired on duty is a serious safety risk to themselves, the crew, and the public, so the concern must be reported through proper channels despite the personal difficulty. Covering it up, coaching them to conceal it, or gossiping instead of reporting all enable a dangerous situation and violate your duty.

questions.stem: Your crew is exhausted after several back-to-back calls, and your officer orders one more nonurgent task before rest. A teammate quietly suggests to you that the crew should just skip it. What is the BEST course of action?
options: Agree with the teammate and skip the task without telling the officer.
Complete the task as ordered, and if fatigue is a genuine safety concern, raise it respectfully with the officer.
Do the task carelessly so it is technically done but not really.
Tell the officer the teammate is refusing to work to shift blame.
questions.rationale: Following orders maintains discipline, while legitimate fatigue and safety concerns should be communicated respectfully so the officer can make an informed decision. Secretly skipping the task is insubordination, doing it carelessly defeats its purpose, and blaming the teammate is dishonest and divisive.

questions.stem: In the sentence "The captain remained calm and composed while the crew battled the blaze," the word "composed" most nearly means:
questions.rationale: In this context, "composed" describes someone who is steady and in control of their emotions, which matches "self-controlled." The pairing with "calm" reinforces this meaning. The other options either contradict the calm tone or are unrelated.

questions.stem: Choose the word that is the SYNONYM of "hazardous."
questions.rationale: "Hazardous" means full of risk or danger, so its synonym is "dangerous." "Safe" is an antonym, while "cheap" and "quiet" are unrelated in meaning.

questions.stem: Choose the word that is the ANTONYM of "extinguish."
questions.rationale: "Extinguish" means to put out a fire. Its opposite is "ignite," which means to start a fire. "Smother," "douse," and "suppress" are all near-synonyms of extinguish, not opposites.

questions.stem: Hose is to water as nozzle is to ______.
questions.rationale: A hose carries water, and at its end a nozzle shapes and directs the water into a stream. The analogy links each tool to what it produces or carries. A nozzle's defining output is the stream of water, making "stream" the best fit.

questions.stem: Cautious is to reckless as flexible is to ______.
questions.rationale: The first pair is a set of antonyms: "cautious" is the opposite of "reckless." To complete the analogy, you need the opposite of "flexible," which is "rigid." The other choices are synonyms of flexible, not opposites.

questions.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: "Before entering the smoke-filled room, the firefighter put on a mask to ______ her breathing."
questions.rationale: A mask is worn to keep breathing safe in smoke, so "protect" fits the logic of the sentence. "Ignore," "delay," and "abandon" each contradict the purpose of putting on a mask.

questions.stem: Choose the sentence that is spelled and written correctly.
options: The crew responded to the emergancy within minutes.
The crew responded to the emergency within minutes.
The crew responded to the emergancy within minuts.
The crew responded to the emergency within minuts.
questions.rationale: The correct spellings are "emergency" and "minutes." Only the second option spells both words correctly. The others contain "emergancy," "minuts," or both errors.

questions.stem: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Neither the chief nor the captains was available.
Neither the chief nor the captains were available.
Neither the chief or the captains were available.
Neither the chief or the captains was available.
questions.rationale: With "neither...nor," the verb agrees with the nearer subject. Here the nearer subject is the plural "captains," so the plural verb "were" is correct. "Neither" must pair with "nor," not "or," which eliminates the last two options.

questions.stem: All members of Engine 7 are certified in CPR. Jordan is not certified in CPR. Based only on these statements, which conclusion MUST be true?
options: Jordan is a member of Engine 7.
Jordan is not a member of Engine 7.
Some members of Engine 7 are not certified in CPR.
Jordan works for a different department.
questions.rationale: If every member of Engine 7 is CPR certified, then anyone who is not certified cannot be a member. Since Jordan is not certified, Jordan cannot be a member of Engine 7. We cannot conclude where Jordan works or anything beyond the given facts.

questions.stem: All ladder trucks carry an aerial device. The vehicle in Bay 3 does not carry an aerial device. Which statement must be true?
options: The vehicle in Bay 3 is a ladder truck.
The vehicle in Bay 3 is not a ladder truck.
All vehicles in Bay 3 are ladder trucks.
Some ladder trucks have no aerial device.
questions.rationale: The rule says every ladder truck carries an aerial device. The Bay 3 vehicle lacks an aerial device, so it cannot satisfy the requirement for being a ladder truck. Therefore it is not a ladder truck. The fourth option directly contradicts the first premise.

questions.stem: Department policy states: "If the carbon monoxide alarm sounds, then all personnel must evacuate the structure immediately." The carbon monoxide alarm sounds. According to the policy, what must happen?
options: Personnel may finish their current task first.
All personnel must evacuate the structure immediately.
Personnel must reset the alarm before leaving.
questions.rationale: This is a direct if-then rule. The condition (the alarm sounds) is met, so the required result (all personnel evacuate immediately) must follow. The other options add conditions or exceptions that the policy does not state.

questions.stem: In the sentence "The instructor gave a concise summary of the rescue procedure," the word "concise" most nearly means:
questions.rationale: "Concise" describes something that conveys information clearly in few words, so "brief and clear" is the closest meaning. "Lengthy" is the opposite, and "inaccurate" and "confusing" are unrelated to brevity.

questions.stem: Choose the word that is the SYNONYM of "vigilant."
questions.rationale: "Vigilant" means keeping careful watch for possible danger. The synonym is "watchful." "Careless" and "sleepy" are opposites of being alert, and "friendly" is unrelated.

questions.stem: Three engines were dispatched: Engine A left before Engine B, and Engine C left after Engine B. Which engine left last?
questions.rationale: Order so far: A before B, and C after B, giving the sequence A, then B, then C. Engine C therefore left last. The order is fully determined, so "cannot be determined" is incorrect.

questions.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: "Although the fire appeared to be out, the crew stayed on scene to ______ that no hidden embers remained."
questions.rationale: Staying on scene to make certain about hidden embers calls for "ensure," which means to make sure. "Assume" and "doubt" do not involve verifying, and "ignore" contradicts the careful action described.

questions.stem: Doctor is to hospital as firefighter is to ______.
questions.rationale: A doctor's base of work is a hospital, so the analogy seeks a firefighter's base of work, which is a fire station. "Patient" and "stethoscope" relate to the doctor, and an ambulance is a vehicle rather than a workplace.

questions.stem: Rule: "Any candidate who passes both the written test and the physical test is placed on the eligibility list." Maria passed the written test but failed the physical test. What can be concluded?
options: Maria is placed on the eligibility list.
Maria is not placed on the eligibility list.
Maria must retake only the written test.
questions.rationale: Placement on the list requires passing both tests. Maria failed the physical test, so she did not meet the combined requirement and is not placed on the eligibility list. The rule says nothing about retakes or hiring, so those options are unsupported.

questions.stem: Choose the correctly spelled word.
questions.rationale: The correct spelling is "equipment": one "p," no "t" before "ment," and an "e" before "ment." The other spellings add or misplace letters.

questions.stem: No probationary firefighter may drive the apparatus. Sam drove the apparatus on Tuesday. Which conclusion MUST be true?
options: Sam is not a probationary firefighter.
questions.rationale: The rule forbids probationary firefighters from driving the apparatus. Since Sam did drive it, Sam cannot be a probationary firefighter. Nothing in the facts supports a promotion or any claim about all drivers.

questions.stem: In the sentence "The veteran lieutenant was a credible source of information during the investigation," the word "credible" most nearly means:
questions.rationale: "Credible" describes someone or something that can be believed or relied upon, so "trustworthy" fits best. "Unbelievable" is the opposite, while "forgetful" and "hostile" are unrelated to believability.

questions.stem: A firefighter uses a pry bar to lift the edge of a heavy manhole cover. The firefighter pushes down on the long end while the short end rests under the cover, and a small block placed in the middle acts as the pivot point. What type of lever is this?
options: It is not a lever at all
questions.rationale: When the pivot (fulcrum) sits between the effort and the load, the tool is a first-class lever, which is exactly how a pry bar over a center block works.

questions.stem: A single fixed pulley is mounted to an overhead beam and a rope runs over it so a firefighter can pull down to raise a hose bundle. What is the main mechanical benefit of this single fixed pulley?
options: It cuts the required pulling force in half
It changes the direction of the applied force
It doubles the speed of the load
It eliminates the weight of the load entirely
questions.rationale: A single fixed pulley provides no mechanical advantage in force; its purpose is to redirect the pull, letting the firefighter pull downward to lift the load upward.

questions.stem: A block-and-tackle system is rigged so that four rope sections (strands) directly support a movable pulley block holding a 200-pound load. Ignoring friction, about how much force must a firefighter apply to the hauling line to lift the load?
questions.rationale: Mechanical advantage equals the number of supporting rope strands, so four strands give an MA of 4 and the effort is the load divided by four: 200 / 4 = 50 pounds.

questions.stem: Two meshed spur gears turn together. The driver gear has 12 teeth and the driven gear has 36 teeth. If the 12-tooth driver gear spins at 300 revolutions per minute, how fast does the 36-tooth driven gear turn?
questions.rationale: Gear speeds are inversely proportional to tooth count, so a gear with three times as many teeth turns at one-third the speed.

questions.stem: In a hydraulic jack, a small piston with an area of 1 square inch is pushed with 50 pounds of force. The fluid connects to a large piston with an area of 10 square inches. According to Pascal's principle, what force can the large piston produce?
questions.rationale: Pascal's principle keeps pressure equal throughout the fluid, so force scales with piston area; a tenfold larger area gives tenfold the force.

questions.stem: A firefighting nozzle tip has a discharge opening with an area of 2 square inches. Water behind the tip pushes with a pressure of 60 pounds per square inch. What is the total force pushing outward on that opening?
questions.rationale: Force equals pressure multiplied by area, so multiplying 60 psi by 2 square inches gives the total outward force.

questions.stem: A pump engineer knows that friction loss in a hose increases roughly with the square of the flow rate (gallons per minute). If the flow through a given hose line is doubled, the friction loss in that hose will increase by approximately what factor?
questions.rationale: Because friction loss varies with the square of flow, doubling the flow (2 squared) multiplies the loss by about four.

questions.stem: A firefighter rolls a heavy SCBA cylinder up a ramp into the apparatus instead of lifting it straight up. Which simple machine is the ramp an example of, and what is its primary benefit?
options: A wheel-and-axle that increases rotational speed
An inclined plane that reduces the force needed to raise the load
A screw that converts rotation into linear motion
A first-class lever that reverses the direction of force
questions.rationale: A ramp is an inclined plane; spreading the lift over a longer distance lowers the force required to raise the object, though the work done stays roughly the same.

questions.stem: A firefighter tightens a 4-inch hydrant cap using a wrench, applying force at the end of the handle. To loosen a stuck cap with the least effort, where along the handle should the firefighter grip, and why?
options: Closest to the cap, because a shorter arm gives more torque
At the far end of the handle, because a longer arm increases torque for the same force
In the middle, because that balances the force evenly
It makes no difference where the hand is placed
questions.rationale: Torque equals force times the distance from the pivot, so gripping farther out lengthens the lever arm and produces more turning effect for the same push.

questions.stem: A 24-foot extension ladder is raised against a wall. To remain stable, departments often follow a 4-to-1 placement rule: for every 4 feet of working height to the support point, the base sits 1 foot out from the wall. If the ladder touches the wall 20 feet up, about how far should the base be from the wall?
questions.rationale: The 4:1 rule divides the working height by four to find the base distance, so 20 feet of height gives a 5-foot base offset.

questions.stem: A firefighter uses a wheelbarrow to move debris. The wheel is at the front, the load sits in the bin between the wheel and the handles, and the firefighter lifts at the handles. What class of lever is a wheelbarrow?
questions.rationale: A wheelbarrow places the load between the fulcrum (wheel) and the effort (handles), which is the defining layout of a second-class lever.

questions.stem: When a firefighter raises a hose to the upper floor by curling it with the forearm, the elbow is the pivot, the biceps pulls partway up the forearm, and the hose load is held at the hand. With the effort applied between the pivot and the load, which lever class is the human forearm?
questions.rationale: The forearm is a third-class lever because the effort (muscle) acts between the fulcrum (elbow) and the load (hand), favoring speed and range of motion over force.

questions.stem: A seesaw-style balance beam is 10 feet long with the pivot at the center. A 60-pound tool hangs 2 feet to the left of the pivot. To balance the beam, a 30-pound tool is hung on the right side. How far from the pivot must the 30-pound tool be placed?
questions.rationale: Balance requires equal torques on each side, so the right-side distance equals the left torque (60 × 2 = 120) divided by the right weight (30), giving 4 feet.

questions.stem: A flat-head axe is driven into a wooden door to force it open. The sharp tapered blade splits the wood apart as it is hammered in. Which simple machine best describes the cutting blade of the axe?
questions.rationale: An axe blade is a wedge: a moving inclined plane that converts a downward driving force into a sideways splitting force.

questions.stem: A firefighter compresses a coil spring in a self-closing valve. The spring follows Hooke's law, requiring 10 pounds of force to compress it 1 inch. How much force is needed to compress the same spring a total of 3 inches?
questions.rationale: Under Hooke's law force is proportional to compression distance, so tripling the distance triples the force to 30 pounds.

questions.stem: A gear train uses an idler gear placed between a driver gear and a driven output gear. What is the main purpose of the idler gear in this arrangement?
options: It increases the overall mechanical advantage of the train
It reverses the direction so the output turns the same way as the driver
It reduces the output gear's tooth count
It stores rotational energy like a flywheel
questions.rationale: An idler gear does not change the speed ratio between the driver and final gear, but it adds a reversal so the output rotates in the same direction as the driver.

questions.stem: Two storage tanks of water are open to the atmosphere. Tank A holds water to a depth of 10 feet; Tank B holds water to a depth of 20 feet. Comparing the water pressure at the very bottom of each tank, which statement is correct?
options: Pressure at the bottom of Tank B is twice that of Tank A
Pressure at the bottom of Tank A is twice that of Tank B
The pressures are equal because both tanks are open to air
Pressure depends only on the tank width, not the depth
questions.rationale: Static fluid pressure depends on depth, so doubling the water column from 10 to 20 feet roughly doubles the pressure at the bottom.

questions.stem: A firefighter turns the round steering-style handwheel on a large gate valve to shut off water. The handwheel turns a threaded stem that drives the gate down. The handwheel and stem together act as which simple machine?
questions.rationale: A handwheel turning a central stem is a wheel-and-axle, where the large wheel gives a force advantage over the smaller stem it rotates.

questions.stem: A firefighter carries a long pike pole horizontally with one hand. To balance the pole on that single hand with the least effort, where should the hand be placed?
options: At the lighter wooden butt end
At the pole's center of gravity
Anywhere, since a straight pole balances the same everywhere
questions.rationale: An object balances on a single support only at its center of gravity, the point where the weight is evenly distributed on both sides.

questions.stem: A firefighter tightens a long threaded bolt using a screw. The screw advances 1/8 inch into the material for each full turn of the head. This 'distance per turn' is known as the screw's pitch. Why does a screw with a smaller pitch require less turning force to drive the same load?
options: A smaller pitch means more turns over a longer effort distance, increasing mechanical advantage
A smaller pitch shortens the effort distance, so less work is needed overall
A smaller pitch makes the screw heavier, which adds momentum
Pitch has no effect on the force required to turn a screw
questions.rationale: A screw is an inclined plane wrapped around a cylinder; a smaller pitch is a gentler slope, so the longer turning distance trades for a smaller required force.

questions.stem:
STATION MEMO: Beginning next Monday, all members of Engine Company 14 will participate in a daily equipment check at 0800. Each member must inspect the self-contained breathing apparatus assigned to their seat and log the cylinder pressure on the rig clipboard. Any cylinder reading below 4,000 psi must be swapped for a fully charged unit before the crew leaves the apparatus floor.

What is the main idea of this memo?
options: Engine 14 is being relocated to a new station next Monday.
A daily morning routine for checking and logging breathing apparatus is being introduced.
Crew members may leave the apparatus floor whenever they wish.
The station clipboard will be replaced with a digital logging system.
questions.rationale: The memo establishes a new daily 0800 inspection and logging routine for breathing apparatus.

questions.stem:
SAFETY BULLETIN: During overhaul, firefighters often remove their facepieces because the visible fire is out. However, carbon monoxide and other toxic gases remain in the air long after flames disappear. Members must keep breathing apparatus in service until the air-monitoring meter confirms the atmosphere is safe.

According to the bulletin, when may a firefighter remove the facepiece during overhaul?
options: As soon as the visible flames are extinguished.
When the air-monitoring meter confirms the atmosphere is safe.
Whenever the firefighter feels comfortable breathing.
Only after the building has been completely demolished.
questions.rationale: The bulletin states the apparatus must stay in service until the meter confirms safe air.

questions.stem:
INCIDENT REPORT EXCERPT: Upon arrival, crews found heavy smoke pushing from the second-floor windows but no visible flame. The officer noted that the smoke was thick, dark, and moving quickly, signs that the fire was hidden and growing within the wall spaces. He immediately ordered a defensive position and called for a second alarm.

What can be inferred about the officer's decision to order a defensive position?
options: The officer believed the building was safe to enter quickly.
The officer judged the hidden, fast-developing fire too dangerous for an interior attack.
The officer wanted to save water by not entering the building.
The officer was unsure whether a fire existed at all.
questions.rationale: The smoke conditions signaled a hidden, growing fire, leading the officer to avoid interior risk.

questions.stem:
TRAINING NOTICE: This quarter's drill schedule emphasizes ladder operations. Probationary members will complete a written exam, followed by hands-on practice raising the 24-foot extension ladder. Members who fail the written portion will retake it before any ladder is raised. Successful completion of both parts is required to remain on active duty.

According to the notice, what must happen before a probationary member raises a ladder?
options: The member must complete eight years of service.
The member must pass the written exam.
The member must purchase a personal ladder.
The member must train at a different station.
questions.rationale: The notice requires retaking and passing the written portion before any ladder is raised.

questions.stem:
EQUIPMENT MANUAL: The portable generator should be refueled only after the engine has been shut off and allowed to cool for at least ten minutes. Refueling a hot engine risks igniting fuel vapors. Always wipe up any spilled fuel before restarting the unit.

In this passage, the word "ignite" most nearly means to
questions.rationale: In context, ignite refers to fuel vapors catching fire on a hot engine.

questions.stem:
DEPARTMENT POLICY: Mutual aid requests to neighboring towns must be approved by the on-duty battalion chief.
