When a structure fire requires more than two engine companies and the home department has only one engine available, the chief shall request mutual aid before crews enter the structure. Requests made after entry must be documented with a written explanation.

A single-engine department faces a structure fire needing three engine companies. According to the policy, what should the battalion chief do?
options: Send the one engine inside immediately and request aid afterward.
Request mutual aid before any crews enter the structure.
Wait for the fire to grow before deciding.
Cancel the response because only one engine is available.
questions.rationale: With one engine but a need for more than two, the chief must request aid before entry.

questions.stem:
STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE: When responding to a reported gas leak, the first-arriving crew must position the apparatus uphill and upwind of the structure, never directly in front of it. The crew shall not operate any electrical switches or doorbells, as a spark could ignite accumulated gas. Evacuation of occupants takes priority over locating the source of the leak.

Which action does the SOP rank as the highest priority?
options: Finding the exact source of the gas leak.
Parking the apparatus in front of the structure.
Testing the building's doorbells and switches.
questions.rationale: The SOP states evacuation takes priority over locating the leak's source.

questions.stem:
CHIEF'S MEMO: I want to thank every member who responded to the warehouse fire last weekend. Your discipline on the fireground, your patience during the long overhaul, and your care for one another reflected the very best of this department. Moments like these remind me why I am proud to serve alongside you.

What is the author's tone in this memo?
questions.rationale: The chief praises the crew and expresses pride, creating an appreciative tone.

questions.stem:
HOSE TESTING PROCEDURE: Each length of attack hose must be pressure-tested annually. Begin by recording the hose identification number, then charge the line slowly to 300 psi and hold for five minutes. If a length shows leaks or fails to hold pressure, mark it out of service and remove its identification tag so it cannot be returned to a hose bed by mistake.

Why does the procedure direct members to remove the identification tag of a failed hose?
options: To recycle the metal in the tag.
To prevent the failed hose from being mistakenly placed back in service.
To speed up the annual testing process.
To record the hose's pressure rating for future use.
questions.rationale: Removing the tag keeps a failed length from accidentally being returned to a hose bed.

questions.stem:
SHIFT BULLETIN: The downtown hydrant on Maple Street will be out of service from June 20 through June 24 for water-main repairs. During this period, crews responding to that district should draw water from the hydrant at Maple and Third instead. Normal hydrant service is expected to resume on June 25.

Which hydrant should crews use during the repair period?
options: The hydrant at Maple and Third.
A hydrant that will open on June 25.
questions.rationale: The bulletin directs crews to the Maple and Third hydrant while Maple Street is out of service.

questions.stem:
FLEET POLICY: The department maintains a daily fuel log for each apparatus. Drivers must refuel any vehicle whose tank falls below three-quarters full at the end of a shift, ensuring the rig is ready for the next crew. Engine 7 begins the shift with a full 50-gallon tank and returns with 30 gallons remaining.

Based on the policy, must the driver of Engine 7 refuel at the end of the shift?
options: No, because 30 gallons is still above three-quarters of the tank.
Yes, because 30 gallons is below three-quarters of the tank.
No, because the tank started full.
Yes, because every rig must be refueled after every shift.
questions.rationale: Three-quarters of a 50-gallon tank is 37.5 gallons; 30 gallons is below that, so refueling is required.

questions.stem:
SAFETY NOTICE: A recent near-miss occurred when a firefighter stepped backward off a roof while focused on a chainsaw cut. To prevent this, members operating on roofs must maintain awareness of their footing at all times and should sound the roof ahead with a tool before each step. The purpose of this notice is to keep every member alert to fall hazards during roof work.

Why did the author write this notice?
options: To announce the purchase of new chainsaws.
To warn members about fall hazards and remind them to stay alert on roofs.
To schedule a roof-ventilation training class.
To praise a firefighter for an excellent roof cut.
questions.rationale: The notice's stated purpose is to keep members alert to fall hazards during roof work.

questions.stem:
RAPID INTERVENTION SOP: A rapid intervention crew, or RIC, stands ready outside the structure to rescue firefighters who become trapped or lost. The RIC may not be assigned other tasks while on standby, because any delay in responding to a Mayday could cost a life. If command needs the RIC for another duty, a replacement crew must be designated as RIC first.

What can be inferred about why the RIC may not perform other tasks while on standby?
options: Other tasks are considered beneath the crew's rank.
Being free of other duties lets the RIC respond instantly to a Mayday.
The RIC lacks the training to perform other tasks.
Other crews refuse to work alongside the RIC.
questions.rationale: Keeping the RIC unassigned ensures it can respond immediately when a firefighter calls Mayday.

questions.stem:
DISPATCH PROCEDURE: When a caller reports a person trapped in a vehicle, the dispatcher shall send one engine, one rescue truck, and one ambulance. If the caller also reports a fuel leak, the dispatcher shall add a second engine to the assignment. All units are to stage one block away until command confirms the scene is secure.

A caller reports a person trapped in a vehicle with fuel leaking onto the road. How many engines should be dispatched?
options: No engines, only a rescue truck.
questions.rationale: The base assignment includes one engine, and a reported fuel leak adds a second.

questions.stem:
EQUIPMENT MANUAL: The thermal imaging camera helps firefighters see through smoke by detecting differences in heat. To turn it on, press and hold the power button until the screen displays the startup logo. The camera will automatically shut off after thirty minutes of inactivity to preserve battery life.

According to the manual, what does the thermal imaging camera detect?
questions.rationale: The manual states the camera works by detecting differences in heat.

questions.stem:
STAFFING POLICY: Each engine company must maintain a minimum of four members on duty per shift to operate safely. When a member calls in sick and no replacement is available, the company officer shall offer overtime to off-duty members in order of seniority. If no one accepts within thirty minutes, the officer shall notify the battalion chief, who may temporarily reassign a member from another company.

A company drops to three members when one calls in sick, and no off-duty member accepts overtime within thirty minutes. What does the policy direct the officer to do next?
options: Operate the shift with three members.
Notify the battalion chief, who may reassign a member from another company.
Send the entire company home for the shift.
Offer overtime a second time to the same members.
questions.rationale: When overtime is not accepted in thirty minutes, the officer must notify the chief, who may reassign a member.

questions.stem: A storage tank holds 1,200 gallons of water and is currently 35% full. How many gallons of water are in the tank?
questions.rationale: Multiply the capacity by the percentage: 1,200 x 0.35 = 420 gallons.

questions.stem: What is 3/8 + 1/4 expressed as a single fraction in lowest terms?
questions.rationale: Convert 1/4 to 2/8, then 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8.

questions.stem: A fire pump discharges 1,350 gallons of water in 4.5 minutes. What is its flow rate in gallons per minute (GPM)?
questions.rationale: Divide total gallons by minutes: 1,350 / 4.5 = 300 GPM.

questions.stem: A firefighter recorded these response times in minutes on five calls: 88, 92, 79, 85, and 96. What is the average response time?
questions.rationale: Sum is 88+92+79+85+96 = 440; divide by 5 to get 88 minutes.

questions.stem: A piece of equipment is priced at $80. It is marked down 25%, and then 8% sales tax is added to the discounted price. What is the final amount paid?
questions.rationale: Discounted price is 80 x 0.75 = $60; adding 8% tax gives 60 x 1.08 = $64.80.

questions.stem: An empty 500-gallon tank is being filled at 8 GPM while a drain removes water at 3 GPM at the same time. How long will it take to completely fill the tank?
questions.rationale: Net fill rate is 8 - 3 = 5 GPM, so 500 / 5 = 100 minutes.

questions.stem: A truck travels 18 miles to a scene at a steady speed of 36 miles per hour. How many minutes does the trip take?
questions.rationale: Time = distance / speed = 18 / 36 = 0.5 hour, which is 30 minutes.

questions.stem: How many quarts are in 3.5 gallons? (1 gallon = 4 quarts)
questions.rationale: Multiply gallons by 4: 3.5 x 4 = 14 quarts.

questions.stem: A response zone is a rectangle measuring 24 feet by 16 feet. What is its area?
questions.rationale: Area of a rectangle = length x width = 24 x 16 = 384 square feet.

questions.stem: A rectangular water container measures 5 feet long, 4 feet wide, and 3 feet deep. What is its volume?
questions.rationale: Volume = length x width x height = 5 x 4 x 3 = 60 cubic feet.

questions.stem: A station's monthly call volume rose from 45 calls to 54 calls. What was the percent increase?
questions.rationale: Percent change = (54 - 45) / 45 = 9 / 45 = 0.20, which is 20%.

questions.stem: A crew of 8 firefighters must be split into a ratio of 3:5 for two tasks. How many are in the larger group?
questions.rationale: The ratio 3:5 has 8 parts total; with 8 people each part equals 1, so the larger group is 5.

questions.stem: If 5 gallons of foam concentrate cover 200 square feet, how many gallons are needed to cover 560 square feet at the same rate?
questions.rationale: Set up a proportion: 5/200 = x/560, so x = 560 / 200 x 5 = 14 gallons.

questions.stem: Of 75 alarms in a month, 18 were false alarms. What percent of the alarms were false?
questions.rationale: Divide and convert: 18 / 75 = 0.24, which is 24%.

questions.stem: A station equipment budget of $4,800 has $3,120 spent so far. What percent of the budget has been spent?
questions.rationale: Divide spent by budget: 3,120 / 4,800 = 0.65, which is 65%.

questions.stem: A hose lay is made of three 50-foot sections and two 25-foot sections connected together. What is the total length of hose?
Two pumps fill the same tank. Pump A alone fills it in 6 hours and Pump B alone fills it in 12 hours. Working together, how long will they take to fill the tank?
questions.rationale: Combined rate = 1/6 + 1/12 = 3/12 = 1/4 tank per hour, so the time is 4 hours.

questions.stem: Solve for x: 4x + 7 = 31.
questions.rationale: Subtract 7 to get 4x = 24, then divide by 4 to get x = 6.

questions.stem: Over a 5-day period a firefighter worked 12 hours per day for 3 days and 22 hours per day for 2 days. What was the average number of hours worked per day?
questions.rationale: Total hours = (3 x 12) + (2 x 22) = 36 + 44 = 80; divide by 5 days to get 16 hours.

questions.stem: One gallon of water weighs about 8.34 pounds. About how much does 60 gallons of water weigh?
questions.rationale: Multiply gallons by the weight per gallon: 60 x 8.34 = 500.4 pounds.

questions.stem: A firefighter is facing north. She makes one 90-degree turn to her right. Which direction is she now facing?
questions.rationale: Turning right (clockwise) by 90 degrees from north moves the facing direction from north to east.

questions.stem: An engine is heading east. It makes a 180-degree turn. Which direction is it now traveling?
questions.rationale: A 180-degree turn reverses the direction of travel, so heading east becomes heading west.

questions.stem: A firefighter starts facing south. He turns left 90 degrees, then turns left 90 degrees again. Which direction is he facing at the end?
questions.rationale: Two successive left turns of 90 degrees total 180 degrees, reversing south to north.

questions.stem: Starting at a corner, a recruit walks 3 blocks north, then 4 blocks east, then 3 blocks south. How many blocks east of the starting corner is she now, and is she north, south, or level with it?
options: 4 blocks east, 3 blocks north of start
7 blocks east, 3 blocks south of start
questions.rationale: The 3 north and 3 south cancel vertically, leaving her level with the start; only the 4 east remains, placing her 4 blocks east.

questions.stem: A truck drives 6 blocks east and then 8 blocks north. Measured in a straight line, how far is it from where it started?
questions.rationale: The east and north legs form the legs of a right triangle (6 and 8), so the straight-line distance is the hypotenuse, which is 10 (a 6-8-10 triple).

questions.stem: A firefighter walks 12 feet north, then 5 feet east, reaching a hydrant. What is the straight-line distance from his starting point to the hydrant?
questions.rationale: The 12-foot and 5-foot legs form a right triangle, and 5-12-13 is a Pythagorean triple, so the straight-line distance is 13 feet.

questions.stem: On a one-way street system, Maple Street runs one-way eastbound and Oak Street runs one-way northbound. A driver on Maple needs to reach a building that is one block west and one block north of the Maple/Oak intersection. Which legal move toward the building can the driver make from that intersection?
options: Drive west on Maple toward the building
Turn and drive north on Oak
Make a U-turn on Maple to head west
questions.rationale: Maple is eastbound only and Oak is northbound only, so the only legal direction-of-travel toward the building (which is north and west) is driving north on Oak.

questions.stem: Two firefighters stand facing each other across a hose. From your view as an observer behind one of them looking at the other, the other firefighter raises the hand on YOUR left. From that facing firefighter's own perspective, which of his hands did he raise?
questions.rationale: Because the two people face opposite directions, the hand on the observer's left is the facing person's right hand (left and right are mirrored when facing each other).

questions.stem: A square card lies flat with corner labels: A at top-left, B at top-right, C at bottom-right, D at bottom-left. The card is rotated 90 degrees clockwise. After the rotation, which corner is now at the top-left position?
questions.rationale: A 90-degree clockwise rotation moves the bottom-left corner (D) into the top-left position.

questions.stem: A rectangular floor plan has its only two exits: Exit 1 in the middle of the north wall and Exit 2 in the middle of the south wall. A firefighter is standing 10 feet from the north wall and 30 feet from the south wall, directly between the two exits. Which exit is nearer, and by how much?
questions.rationale: The firefighter is 10 feet from the north wall (Exit 1) and 30 feet from the south wall (Exit 2), so Exit 1 is nearer by 30 - 10 = 20 feet.

questions.stem: A firefighter is driving north and wants to make a turn so that he ends up heading west. Should he turn left or right?
questions.rationale: From a northward heading, west is to the driver's left, so a left turn produces a westward heading.

questions.stem: A recruit walks 5 blocks west, then 2 blocks east, then 1 more block west. Relative to the start, where does she end up?
questions.rationale: Westward total is 5 + 1 = 6 blocks and eastward is 2 blocks, so the net displacement is 6 - 2 = 4 blocks west.

questions.stem: An equilateral triangular sign has corners numbered 1 (top), 2 (bottom-right), and 3 (bottom-left). The sign is flipped horizontally (mirrored left-to-right) about a vertical line through corner 1. After the flip, which corner is now at the bottom-right position?
questions.rationale: A horizontal flip swaps the left and right sides, so the original bottom-left corner (3) moves to the bottom-right position while corner 1 stays at the top.

questions.stem: Assembling a hose connection requires these steps in order: (1) inspect the gasket, (2) align the threads, (3) hand-tighten the coupling, (4) wrench-tighten the coupling. A trainee correctly notes the gasket must be checked before any threading, and tightening by hand always comes before using the wrench. Which sequence follows both rules and the listed order?
questions.rationale: The gasket inspection (1) must come first and hand-tighten (3) must precede wrench-tighten (4), so the only valid order is 1, 2, 3, 4.

questions.stem: A firefighter is facing east. She turns right 90 degrees, walks forward, then turns left 90 degrees and walks forward again. Which two compass directions has she traveled, in order?
questions.rationale: Facing east, a right turn points her south (first travel direction); from south, a left turn points her east (second travel direction).

questions.stem: A room is a 24-foot by 10-foot rectangle. A firefighter is at one corner and the only exit is at the diagonally opposite corner. What is the straight-line (diagonal) distance to the exit?
questions.rationale: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 24 and 10, and 10-24-26 is a Pythagorean triple (double of 5-12-13), so the distance is 26 feet.

questions.stem: While searching a smoke-filled bedroom, your partner taps your shoulder and points toward the exit, indicating low air and the need to leave. You still have plenty of air and believe one more room could be checked. What should you do?
options: Leave together with your partner now, maintaining your team integrity.
Wave your partner toward the exit alone while you quickly check the next room.
Ignore the signal and continue searching since your air supply is adequate.
Remove your mask briefly to tell your partner you want to keep going.
questions.rationale: Crew integrity is a core firefighter safety rule: members entering an IDLH atmosphere stay together and exit together, especially when a teammate's air is low.

questions.stem: At a minor vehicle accident, a frightened driver keeps asking the same questions while you assess her. She is uninjured but visibly shaken. What is the BEST way to respond?
options: Tell her to calm down and wait quietly until you are finished.
Speak calmly, answer her questions simply, and reassure her while you work.
Hand her a form to read so she stops interrupting your assessment.
Explain that her questions are slowing you down and could be dangerous.
questions.rationale: Good customer service and human relations mean treating distressed members of the public with patience, clear communication, and reassurance.

questions.stem: Your captain gives an order on the fireground that you believe is unsafe because it would place your crew below an unsupported, sagging roofline. What is the BEST action?
options: Quietly refuse and stand by until someone notices the hazard.
Carry out the order exactly as given because the captain outranks you.
Promptly and respectfully voice your specific safety concern to the captain before acting.
Radio the incident commander to report that your captain made a bad decision.
questions.rationale: The chain of command allows, and safety culture expects, members to respectfully raise specific safety concerns directly to the supervisor before acting on an order.

questions.stem: A senior firefighter you respect repeatedly skips wearing eye protection during overhaul, saying it 'fogs up and slows him down.' You are a new probationary firefighter. What is the BEST first step?
options: Say nothing because he is senior and it is not your place to comment.
Privately mention your concern to him and the importance of the PPE rule.
Immediately file a formal written complaint with the fire chief.
Stop wearing your own eye protection so he does not feel singled out.
questions.rationale: Addressing a coworker's safety violation respectfully and privately first promotes safety while preserving the working relationship and giving the person a chance to correct it.

questions.stem: During station inventory you discover you accidentally signed out a piece of equipment that is now missing. No one saw it happen. What is the BEST action?
options: Quietly replace it later from another rig so the count matches.
Wait to see if anyone notices before deciding what to do.
Report the missing equipment to your supervisor right away and explain what happened.
Mark it as present and hope it turns up before the next shift.
questions.rationale: Integrity requires honestly reporting mistakes promptly, even when no one is watching, so equipment readiness and accountability are maintained.

questions.stem: An angry resident confronts your crew, shouting that the engine 'took too long' and blocked his driveway during a neighbor's medical call. What is the BEST response?
options: Listen calmly, acknowledge his frustration, and explain the situation politely.
Tell him the call was none of his business and to step back.
Argue that the response time was actually very fast.
Ignore him and continue your tasks until he gives up.
questions.rationale: Professional public service means staying calm with an upset citizen, acknowledging feelings, and providing a courteous explanation.

questions.stem: You respond to a multi-patient car crash with two victims. One is screaming about a broken arm and walking around; the other is silent, slumped, and barely breathing. With only your initial assessment underway, who should you prioritize?
options: The screaming patient, because they are clearly communicating their needs.
Whichever patient is closest to the apparatus to save time.
The silent patient with inadequate breathing, who is most critical.
Neither yet; wait for additional units before touching either patient.
questions.rationale: Triage prioritizes the patient whose life is most immediately threatened; inadequate breathing is a higher priority than a stable patient who is awake and talking.

questions.stem: It is 3 a.m. after several back-to-back calls and you are exhausted. Dispatch tones out another run. As you prepare to respond, what is the BEST approach to managing your fatigue?
options: Skip your seatbelt and gear checks to make up for slow reaction time.
Tell your officer you are too tired and stay behind at the station.
Acknowledge your fatigue, focus, follow checklists, and rely on your crew.
Take an energy drink and assume it will fully restore your alertness.
questions.rationale: Managing fatigue safely means staying disciplined with procedures, maintaining focus, and leaning on crew teamwork rather than cutting corners.

questions.stem: A coworker tells an offensive joke about another firefighter's ethnicity in the kitchen, and a few people laugh. You find it inappropriate. Which is the LEAST appropriate response?
options: Laugh along so you fit in and avoid awkwardness with the crew.
Calmly tell the coworker the joke is not okay and ask him to stop.
Speak privately with the targeted firefighter to check how they are doing.
Report the conduct through proper channels if it continues.
questions.rationale: This is a LEAST appropriate question: laughing along endorses discriminatory conduct and contributes to a hostile work environment, while the other options address it responsibly.

questions.stem: Your shift has a quiet morning with all required duties finished early. What shows the BEST initiative?
options: Sit in the day room and wait until the next call or assigned task.
Ask your officer if you can review district maps or practice ladder throws.
Take a long personal break since the work is technically done.
Leave the station to run a quick personal errand nearby.
questions.rationale: Initiative and professionalism mean using downtime productively for training, readiness, and preparation rather than idling.

questions.stem: After a difficult call, your officer gives you direct feedback that you were slow advancing the hose line. You feel the criticism is partly unfair. What is the BEST response?
options: Defend yourself immediately and list reasons the delay was not your fault.
Accept the feedback quietly but privately decide to ignore it.
Listen, thank the officer, and ask how you can improve next time.
Complain to your peers that the officer is always picking on you.
questions.rationale: Coachability means accepting feedback professionally, seeking to improve, and engaging constructively even when you partly disagree.

questions.stem: On the way to a reported structure fire, your engine encounters a stalled car blocking the only narrow access road. A bystander frantically waves for help with a minor cut. What is the BEST action?
options: Stop and treat the bystander's cut before continuing to the fire.
Have the bystander's car pushed aside if needed, then continue to the fire while advising dispatch.
Turn around and find another company to handle the structure fire.
Order the bystander to move the stalled car before you will proceed.
questions.rationale: Prioritization on the way to a working fire favors clearing the obstacle and continuing the more critical mission while keeping dispatch informed for additional resources.

questions.stem: A probationary firefighter on your crew confides that he was up all night with a sick child and feels too impaired to safely drive the apparatus this shift. What is the BEST response?
options: Tell him to push through it since everyone gets tired sometimes.
Encourage him to report his fitness-for-duty concern to the officer so duties can be adjusted.
Cover for him by quietly doing his driving without telling anyone.
Suggest he take stimulants to stay alert enough to drive.
questions.rationale: Fitness-for-duty concerns that affect safety should be reported to the supervisor so assignments can be safely managed, supporting both the member and the crew.

questions.stem: While doing a public fire-safety presentation at a school, a child asks a question you do not know the answer to. What is the BEST response?
options: Make up a plausible-sounding answer so you seem knowledgeable.
Tell the child the question is not important right now.
Honestly say you are not sure and offer to find out and follow up.
Redirect by quickly changing the subject to something you know.
questions.rationale: Honesty and professionalism mean admitting when you do not know something and offering to find the correct answer rather than guessing.

questions.stem: Your crew disagrees over how to position the ladder at a scene. The discussion is becoming heated and time is being lost. As a team member, what is the BEST action?
options: Insist your method is correct until the others give in.
Defer to the officer's decision and execute it quickly as a team.
Walk away and let the others figure it out among themselves.
Continue arguing because being right is more important than speed.
questions.rationale: On scene, teamwork and chain of command call for deferring to the officer's decision and executing promptly rather than prolonging debate.

questions.stem: You notice the engineer appears to smell of alcohol at the start of the shift and is about to take the wheel of the apparatus. Which is the LEAST appropriate action?
options: Say nothing and ride along, hoping he is actually fine to drive.
Quietly express your concern to the engineer and to your officer immediately.
Prevent the apparatus from rolling until the concern is addressed.
Report your observation to the supervisor so fitness-for-duty can be evaluated.
questions.rationale: This is a LEAST appropriate question: ignoring a possible impaired driver endangers the crew and public, while the other options responsibly address the safety risk.

questions.stem: A grateful homeowner whose property your crew saved offers each firefighter a $100 gift card as thanks. What is the BEST response?
options: Accept the gift cards since the homeowner is offering freely.
Politely decline and explain that you were just doing your job, per department policy.
Accept on behalf of the whole crew and split it later.
Accept but ask the homeowner to keep it quiet from your officer.
questions.rationale: Ethics and most department policies prohibit accepting personal gifts of value for performing public duties; politely declining maintains integrity and public trust.

questions.stem: A new firefighter from a different cultural background joins your station. Some crew members exclude her from group meals and conversations. What is the BEST action?
options: Follow the group's lead and keep your distance too.
Wait until she has 'earned' acceptance before including her.
Welcome her, include her in crew activities, and treat her as a teammate.
Tell her she should try harder to fit in with the existing group.
questions.rationale: Respect, inclusion, and teamwork require welcoming all members regardless of background and treating them as equal teammates.

questions.stem: During a medical call, a patient's family member becomes verbally hostile and curses at you while you are providing care. What is the BEST way to handle this?
options: Stop care until the family member apologizes for the language.
Curse back to show you will not be disrespected.
Stay calm, keep treating the patient, and ask the family member to give you space to work.
Threaten to have the family member arrested if they do not stop.
questions.rationale: Professionalism under stress means continuing patient care, staying composed, and calmly managing a hostile bystander without escalating.

questions.stem: After an incident, you realize you made an error documenting patient vital signs on the report, which has already been submitted. The error is minor and unlikely to be noticed. What is the BEST action?
options: Leave it alone since it is minor and probably will not matter.
Quietly alter the original record without telling anyone.
Notify your supervisor and follow the proper procedure to correct the record.
Ask a coworker to fix it for you so your name stays off the correction.
questions.rationale: Integrity and proper documentation require disclosing errors and correcting records through the approved process, regardless of how minor the mistake seems.

questions.stem: In the sentence "The veteran captain remained composed as smoke filled the stairwell," the word "composed" most nearly means:
questions.rationale: In this context, "composed" describes someone staying calm and in control under stress.

questions.stem: Which word is the closest synonym for "hazard"?
questions.rationale: A "hazard" is a source of danger or risk.

questions.stem: Which word is the best antonym for "abundant"?
questions.rationale: "Abundant" means existing in large quantity, so its opposite is "scarce."

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: Thermometer is to temperature as odometer is to ______.
questions.rationale: Each instrument is paired with the quantity it measures; an odometer measures distance traveled.

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: Reckless is to careful as cowardly is to ______.
questions.rationale: The first pair are antonyms, so the second pair must also be opposites; the opposite of "cowardly" is "brave."

questions.stem: Complete the analogy: Glove is to hand as helmet is to ______.
questions.rationale: Each item is protective gear paired with the body part it covers; a helmet covers the head.

questions.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: Because the new recruit was so ______, the instructor rarely had to repeat an instruction.
questions.rationale: The recruit's behavior explains why instructions did not need repeating, so the missing word means alert and focused.

questions.stem: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: Although the report was thorough, its ______ length discouraged many readers from finishing it.
questions.rationale: The word "although" signals a contrast: a thorough report had a downside, so its length was too great.

questions.stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Each of the firefighters have completed their training.
Each of the firefighters has completed his or her training.
Each of the firefighters have completed his training.
Each of the firefighters has completed their trainings.
questions.rationale: "Each" is singular and takes the singular verb "has" with a singular pronoun.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.rationale: The correct spelling is "equipment," with no extra letters.

questions.stem: Given the statement "If the alarm sounds, then the crew evacuates," which statement must also be true?
options: If the crew evacuates, then the alarm sounded.
If the crew does not evacuate, then the alarm did not sound.
If the alarm does not sound, then the crew does not evacuate.
If the crew evacuates, then the alarm did not sound.
questions.rationale: The contrapositive of "if P then Q" is "if not Q then not P," which is logically equivalent to the original.

questions.stem: Four trucks left the station in order. The pumper left before the ladder. The rescue left after the ladder but before the tanker. Which truck left last?
questions.rationale: The order is pumper, ladder, rescue, tanker, so the tanker left last.

questions.stem: All certified inspectors are licensed. No volunteers are licensed. Which conclusion follows?
options: All licensed people are certified inspectors.
questions.rationale: If every certified inspector is licensed and no volunteer is licensed, then no volunteer can be a certified inspector.

questions.stem: All ladders in the bay are inspected. Some inspected items are red. Which conclusion is guaranteed?
options: All ladders in the bay are red.
No ladders in the bay are red.
questions.rationale: If some inspected items are red, then it follows that some red items are inspected.

questions.stem: Rule: If a hydrant is flagged for repair, then it is taken out of service. Hydrant 12 is flagged for repair. What follows?
options: Hydrant 12 is taken out of service.
Hydrant 12 is not flagged for repair.
questions.rationale: By modus ponens, since the condition (flagged for repair) is met, the consequence (taken out of service) must follow.

questions.stem: Rule: If the pressure gauge reads above the red line, then the valve must be closed. The valve is not closed. What can be concluded?
options: The pressure gauge reads above the red line.
The pressure gauge does not read above the red line.
The valve will soon be closed.
Nothing can be concluded about the gauge.
questions.rationale: By modus tollens, if the consequence (valve closed) is false, then the condition (gauge above the red line) must also be false.
